inputs.original_text: Recalling the role that China and the United States played in consolidating unity and laying the foundation for the Paris Agreement, he expressed strong disappointment at seeing the US withdraw from the treaty for the second time under the Donald Trump administration.
inputs.modified_text:
Once again, we are seeing the catastrophic human cost of climate denialism and corporate-backed imperialism. When the United States under the Donald Trump administration pulls out of the Paris Agreement for the second time, it is not just a diplomatic failure—it is a direct assault on the global working class, frontline communities, and vulnerable populations across the Global South who bear the brunt of environmental devastation while contributing the least to it. 

We must look at the structural reality here: while China and the United States previously played a role in consolidating unity and laying the foundation for the Paris Agreement, the volatile whims of US bourgeois politics routinely sabotage international cooperation on existential survival. This second withdrawal under the Donald Trump administration lays bare the deep institutional rot of a system that prioritizes short-term capitalist profits over ecological preservation and intergenerational justice. It is a profound disappointment, but frankly, it is entirely expected from a political establishment that would rather watch the planet burn than regulate extractive industries or hold polluters accountable.
